text:
<thought>*   Sanskrit text: "वनम् हि रक्ष्यते व्याघ्रैः व्याघ्रान् रक्षति काननम् न तथा इच्छन्ति अकल्याणाः परेषाम् वेदितुम् गुणान् यथा एषाम् ज्ञातुम् इच्छन्ति नैर्गुण्यम् पाप चेतसः"

    *   *वनम्* (vanam): forest
    *   *हि* (hi): indeed/surely
    *   *रक्ष्यते* (rakshyate): is protected (passive of *raksh*)
    *   *व्याघ्रैः* (vyāghraiḥ): by tigers (instrumental plural)
    *   *व्याघ्रान्* (vyāghrān): tigers (accusative plural)
    *   *रक्षति* (rakshati): protects (active)
    *   *काननम्* (kānanama): forest/grove
    *   *न* (na): not
    *   *तथा* (tathā): so/in that way
    *   *इच्छन्ति* (icchanti): they wish/desire
    *   *अकल्याणाः* (akalyāṇāḥ): those who are not virtuous/wicked people
    *   *परेषाम्* (pareṣām): of others (genitive plural)
    *   *वेदितुम्* (veditum): to know/to perceive (infinitive)
    *   *गुणान्* (guṇān): virtues/qualities (accusative plural)
    *   *यथा* (yathā): as/just as
    *   *एषाम्* (eṣām): of these/their (genitive plural)
    *   *ज्ञातुम्* (jñātum): to know (infinitive)
    *   *इच्छन्ति* (icchanti): they wish/desire
    *   *नैर्गुण्यम्* (nairguṇyam): lack of virtue/vices
    *   *पाप चेतसः* (pāpa cetasaḥ): those with evil minds/sinful-minded people

    *   *Sentence 1:* "वनम् हि रक्ष्यते व्याघ्रैः व्याघ्रान् रक्षति काननम्"
        *   Literal: The forest is indeed protected by tigers; the forest protects the tigers.
        *   Meaning: There is a mutual relationship of protection between the forest and the tigers.

    *   *Sentence 2:* "न तथा इच्छन्ति अकल्याणाः परेषाम् वेदितुम् गुणान् यथा एषाम् ज्ञातुम् इच्छन्ति नैर्गुण्यम् पाप चेतसः"
        *   Literal: Not so do the non-virtuous wish to know the virtues of others, as these evil-minded ones wish to know the lack of virtue.
        *   Refined: Wicked people do not wish to know the virtues of others, just as those with evil minds desire to know their faults.

    *   "The forest is indeed protected by tigers, and the forest protects the tigers. Similarly, the wicked do not wish to know the virtues of others, just as those with evil minds desire to know their faults."

    *   "The forest is indeed protected by tigers, and the forest protects the tigers. In the same way, the wicked do not wish to know the virtues of others, just as those with evil minds desire to know their shortcomings."

    *   "The forest is indeed protected by tigers, and the forest protects the tigers. Similarly, the wicked do not wish to know the virtues of others, just as those with evil minds desire to know their faults."</thought>The forest is indeed protected by tigers, and the forest protects the tigers. Similarly, the wicked do not wish to know the virtues of others, just as those with evil minds desire to know their faults.
